'''''Frullania polysticta''''' is a species of [[Marchantiophyta|liverwort]] in the family [[Frullaniaceae]]. It is found only in [[Madeira]] and the [[Canary Islands]] and is considered a [[vulnerable species]].

==Distribution and habitat==
''Frullania polysticta'' can be found on all islands of both the Madeira and Canary Islands [[archipelago]]s. It is widely distributed across Madeira and is similarly frequent on most of the Canary Islands, though it is rarer on [[Fuerteventura]] and [[Lanzarote]]. It occurs primarily in [[laurel forest]]s at elevations of {{cvt|500-1200|m}} [[above sea level]], occurring most frequently above {{cvt|800|m}}.  It typically grows as an [[epiphyte]] on the bark of trees, but can also be found on shaded rocks and humid soil amongst [[leaf litter]].<ref name=IUCN/>

It has been recorded from the [[Azores]],<ref name=Frullania/> however, these identifications were later determined to be erroneous.<ref name=Azores>{{cite journal |last1=Schumacker |first1=R. |year=2001 |title=The hepatic flora of the Azores: Brief historical outline, present knowledge, endemics and phytogeographical aspects |journal=Belgian Journal of Botany |volume=134 |issue=1 |pages=51–63 |jstor=20794477 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/259854793 |via=[[ResearchGate]]}}</ref>

==Description==
''Frullania polysticta'' is a robust, irregularly branched, mat-forming liverwort that is light green to reddish brown in colour.<ref name=Host>{{cite journal |last1=González-Mancebo |first1=Juana Maria |last2=Losada-Lima |first2=Ana |last3=McAlister |first3=Suzanne |year=2003 |title=Host Specificity of Epiphytic Bryophyte Communities of a Laurel Forest on Tenerife (Canary Islands, Spain) |journal=[[The Bryologist]] |volume=106 |issue=3 |pages=383–394 |doi=10.1639/04 |jstor=3244720 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/232686456 |via=[[ResearchGate]]}}</ref> The shoots measure {{cvt|5-8|cm}} long and {{cvt|1400-2200|um|mm}} wide. The overlapping leaves are borne on stems measuring {{cvt|120-220|um|mm}} in diameter. ''F. polysticta'' is [[dioecious]], with male and female plants being of similar size.<ref name=Frullania/>

''Frullania polysticta'' is a long-lived [[perennial]] species with an estimated [[generation]] length of 11 to 25 years.<ref name=IUCN/> It is the only known host of ''[[Octosporella microtricha]]'', a species of [[parasitic fungus]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Döbbeler |first1=Peter |last2=Berger |first2=Franz |last3=Piñero |first3=Rubén Negrín |last4=Vega |first4=Marcel |year=2018 |title=''Octosporella microtricha'' and ''O. nematospora'' – Two New Pezizalean Ascomycetes on ''Frullania'' |journal=[[Herzogia]] |volume=31 |issue=1 |pages=101–108 |doi=10.13158/099.031.0106 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/326806438 |via=[[ResearchGate]]}}</ref>

==Conservation status==
''Frullania polysticta'' is listed as [[vulnerable species|vulnerable]] on the [[International Union for the Conservation of Nature]]'s [[Red List]] under criterion A3c, based on its decreasing population and observed [[habitat destruction|habitat loss]]. It is threatened by [[urbanization]], [[tourism]], [[overgrazing]], and [[climate change]]. No specific conservation measures are in place to protect this species, however, it is known to occur within [[protected area]]s such as [[Madeira Natural Park]].<ref name=IUCN/>
